elements.label: Figure O.1: Economic growth and poverty reduction, 1993–2020
elements.description: Line chart with two y-axes. Left axis: Poverty rate (%), 0–100. Right axis: GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$), 0–3,000. X-axis: years 1993–2020, shown annually with labels. Legend: Extreme poverty ($1.90/day 2011PPP) (teal); LMIC PL ($3.20/day 2011PPP) (orange); UMIC PL ($5.50/day 2011PPP) (grey); GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$) (yellow). Note: Poverty measurement methodology changed in 2010, rendering a break in series comparability. Source: World Bank WDI, PovcalNet. Approximate readings (~): Extreme poverty: 1993 ~52, 1998 ~31, 2002 ~37, 2004 ~26, 2006 ~19, 2008 ~14, 2010 ~4, 2012 ~2.5, 2014 ~2.4, 2016 ~2, 2018 ~2, 2020 ~1. LMIC PL: 1993 ~80, 1998 ~69, 2002 ~70, 2004 ~60, 2006 ~51, 2008 ~46.5, 2010 ~17, 2012 ~13, 2014 ~11, 2016 ~8, 2018 ~7, 2020 ~5. UMIC PL: 1993 ~94, 1998 ~90, 2002 ~89, 2004 ~85, 2006 ~80, 2008 ~77.5, 2010 ~47.5, 2012 ~41, 2014 ~35, 2016 ~27, 2018 ~23.5, 2020 ~19. GDP per capita (right axis): 1993 ~460, 2002 ~900, 2010 ~1,450, 2020 ~2,600. Poverty rates fall over the period for all lines, with a visible series break around 2008–2010, while GDP per capita rises steadily.

elements.label: Figure O.2: Issues of greatest concern, 2015–2020
elements.description: Grouped vertical bar chart. Y-axis: Percent of respondents, 0–30 (ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30). X-axis: years 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020. Legend: Poverty/Hunger (teal); Economic Growth/GDP (orange); Environment (grey); Health/Insurance (yellow). Approximate values (~): 2015: Poverty/Hunger ~18, Economic Growth/GDP ~4.5, Environment ~2, Health/Insurance ~2.4. 2016: ~24.5, ~7, ~12.5, ~0.9. 2017: ~28.5, ~7.9, ~7.5, ~1.4. 2018: ~25, ~9, ~6.6, ~1.2. 2019: ~24.8, ~10.9, ~8.9, ~1.6. 2020: ~17.8, ~13, ~3.9, ~15.5. Source: CECODES, VFF-CRT, RTA & UNDP (2021). Poverty/Hunger is the largest concern in most years, while Health/Insurance rises sharply in 2020.
